thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall-ml — elevated error rate for smart-routing in eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 fallbacks. Observed ~20% 5xxs and several customers seeing degraded latency. Auto-fallbacks triggered repeatedly.

oncall-ml: I'm up, looking now. Can someone paste the alert and any recent deploys?

sarah-ryan: alert summary: `smart-routing.fallback.loop` 5xx spike aggregated across model routes: gptx-2b, rwd-quant-1. Failures start ~1718001100 and we see repeat fallbacks between eu-west-1 and us-east-1.

omar-ops: no deploys in last 6h from infra. last code deploy was targeted to canary three hours ago by @deploy-bot (id: deploy-7834).

jun-platform: I see a flurry of DNS NX responses from our edge in eu-west-1 for endpoint `inference-us-east-1.redwood-inference.com` — seems like stale endpoint on the edge cache + low TTL propagation issue.

kevin-net: digging into our edge logs: CDN returned cached A records pointing at the older edge IPs for ~90s longer than expected. TTLs should be 30s but some edges cached at 120s due to upstream resolver misbehavior. Could cause traffic to route to wrong region and then trigger fallback policies.

oncall-ml: ok hypothesis: stale DNS at CDN -> requests routed to unexpected region -> smart-routing sees capacity mismatch or incompatible variant -> triggers fallback to another region -> cascading ping-pong. Need to stop loop first.

incident-bot: deploy-bot reports: recent policy change `smartRouting.policy.v2` rolled 4h ago to set `prefer_region: auto` and `fallback_attempts: 3`.

sarah-ryan: that policy change could explain more aggressive fallbacks. If DNS jitter causes temporary mismatch, attempts=3 might create repeated cross-region retries.

natalie-cs: Customer impact: 7 paying customers reported slow/no responses in EU during 1718001100-1718003500. We have two support tickets open, one escalated. ETA on mitigation? Customers want ETA for fix and whether any data loss.

oncall-ml: mitigation plan (immediate):
1) Pause automatic cross-region fallback for affected routes (set `fallback_attempts=0`)
2) Apply traffic pinning to origin region for active connections (force `route: prefer_origin`)
3) Invalidate edge DNS caches / CDN invalidation for inference hostnames
4) Rollback the `prefer_region: auto` flag if safe

jun-platform: executing step 1 and 2 now. Patching runtime policy: ```json
{
  "route_policy": "manual_override",
  "prefer_region": "eu-west-1",
  "fallback_attempts": 0
}
```

deploy-bot: rollout started: policy-patch-1720 -> 4 regions -> 6 nodes.

kevin-net: CDN purge requested for `*.redwood-inference.com` — started. Also triggered a low-level DNS refresh at our authoritative provider (requested preemptive SOA serial bump).

omar-ops: I can see failing clients start to recover once pinned. Error rate drop from 20% to 4% after ~40s of the patch.

incident-bot: oncall handover scheduled in 30m to @oncall-ml (next). Current priority: P0 until fully recovered.

sarah-ryan: root cause timeline (working hypothesis):
- 1718001050: Authoritative DNS updated for some routing changes (normal).
- 1718001080: Edge resolver/cache misapplied TTL and served stale A records for `inference-us-east-1...` to eu-edge.
- 1718001100: Services in eu-west receive traffic destined to US model variants -> model compatibility mismatch -> 5xx or latency -> smart-routing triggers fallback.
- 1718001150-1718001900: Fallbacks escalate due to `fallback_attempts=3` -> loop between regions.

jun-platform: addendum: some model variants are region-locked (rwd-quant-1 only hosted in us-east-1). When DNS routed EU requests to US hostnames but terminated at EU runtime expecting local variant, combination of variant mismatch + header rewrite led to 500s.

natalie-cs: We should prepare a short customer message: "We experienced routing degradation in EU causing timeouts and higher latency for calls to hosted models between 1718001100-1718003500. Mitigations deployed; we're monitoring. No customer data was lost." Can someone confirm?

oncall-ml: Confirmed: no data loss. Models returned errors, but no persisted customer payloads were dropped. Good to send that note.

kevin-net: longer-term fixes to track:
- enforce DNS TTL consistency and add jitter detection alerts
- add guardrail: don't attempt cross-region fallback for region-locked variants
- make `fallback_attempts` dynamic based on recent DNS jitter metric

omar-ops: also recommend: set up a circuit breaker in smart-routing to avoid >N region switches within M seconds (prevents ping-pong).

jun-platform: I'm going to open a follow-up runbook PR with concrete steps: purge CDN, shorten cache TTLs for model endpoints, and add a resolver health check.

incident-bot: remind: POSTMORTEM required within 48h. Severity: P0 -> target follow-up meeting 1718050000.

natalie-cs: support note drafted and sent to affected customers. One customer asked for SLA credit — flagged to finance/sales.

sarah-ryan: after-action checklist (short):
- finalize root cause once DNS provider confirms cache misbehavior
- revert temporary policy overrides after 1h of stable metrics
- add unit/regression test for region-locked variant guardrail
- update monitoring for `dns.cache_consistency` and `routing.pingpong_rate`

oncall-ml: last check: error rate back to baseline, fallbacks suppressed. I'll stay on until handoff. If anything regresses ping me.

deploy-bot: policy-patch-1720 fully rolled. revert window scheduled +10m.

kevin-net: Confirm authoritative provider acknowledged that some edge resolvers ignored the short TTL due to misconfigured upstream peering. They're investigating and will provide postmortem.

natalie-cs: Logging this as incident-1718001234 for tracking and billing implications.

sarah-ryan: Thanks team. Great quick coordination. We'll capture full timeline and mitigations in the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
